items.criterion: Based on experimental connectome data from 64 cell types in the Drosophila visual lobe motor pathway, a hexagonal convolutional recurrent network (DMN) model was constructed. The model assumes spatial translation invariance and periodically tiles the local connectivity graph across the visual field, containing 45,669 neurons and 1,513,231 synapses. By sharing parameters (time constant, resting potential, and unit synaptic strength) for the same cell type, the number of free parameters was reduced from millions theoretically to 734. The model was implemented in PyTorch and can be trained end-to-end for optical flow estimation.

items.criterion: UMAP dimensionality reduction and clustering were performed on the responses of 50 DMNs under natural videos, revealing that the responses of multiple cell types form discrete clusters. Taking T4c as an example, the 50 models were divided into three functional clusters: correct upward selectivity, incorrect downward selectivity, and no directional selectivity. The average task error of the clusters increased in sequence, indicating that models with higher task performance tend to have correct physiological tuning. It was further revealed that the directional preference of T4c is closely coupled with the contrast preference of its input neurons Mi4/Mi9: when Mi4 is of the ON type and Mi9 is of the OFF type, T4c shows upward selectivity; conversely, it shows downward selectivity. This finding provides an effective strategy for constraining whole-brain model parameters by measuring the tuning of a small number of neurons.
